correctness.rationale: Cycle non-guru orientations with no 2-cycle consist precisely of a run of left arrows and a run of right arrows on each guru-to-guru arc. At least two gurus block the only longer directed cycle. This proves independent uniform cutpoints, joint product enumerator and the resulting covariance/candidate vote polynomial. The even two-guru tie count has exactly \(\min(m_0,m_1)+1\) solutions, yielding both sharp bounds. Exact brute force independently checked 1418 configurations with 19966 feasible full assignments, all coefficient and variance identities. All quantifiers and tie boundaries are explicit; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison: Bentert et al. arXiv:2205.05482 explicitly propose counting Winner Determination but supply decision algorithms rather than this cycle enumeration. Utke–Schmidt-Kraepelin arXiv:2307.01174 compute individual branching-to-sink assignments, not the joint law and strict/weak winner coefficients. The others analyze different random graphs or power indices. Targeted searches of published mathematical records on fixed gurus/cycle/uniform branching/root weights/covariance/tie and prior published claims, found no stronger covering theorem. Distinction is statement implication, not just matching terminology; residual bibliography risk remains.
residual_risks: The general directed power watershed/weighted spanning-forest literature may contain unpublished or differently worded explicit cycle consequences; a comprehensive mathematical literature search cannot be guaranteed.
A structural random-arborescence identity could subsume part of the elementary arc enumeration, though no inspected source supplied the ballot-count and sharp tie-extrema results.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly calls for counting delegations that make a candidate a winner, a quantitatively different problem from merely deciding whether one exists. The complete tally polynomial solves it for an infinite natural family, and the variance cut law plus sharp antipodal-vs-adjacent tie extremum quantify uncertainty and positioning in voting networks. These are connected nontrivial structural conclusions, not arbitrary constants; no broad arbitrary-network claim is made.
